context: Interactive 3-panel dashboard showing synthetic earthquake data: a draggable orthographic globe with depth-colored, magnitude-sized circles; a scatter plot of depth vs magnitude with brush selection; and a KDE ridgeline chart of depth distribution by tectonic zone.
first_impression: Structurally honest encoding throughout — scaleSqrt for circle radius, Silverman bandwidth for KDE, zero-baseline areas — but all axis domains are hardcoded magic numbers and the ridgeline legend silently omits two of six tectonic zones.
what_works: Circle radius uses d3.scaleSqrt correctly (area proportional to magnitude); KDE bandwidth uses Silverman's rule making smoothing data-driven rather than arbitrary, and the ridgeline density scale is dynamic so filtering updates proportions correctly.
what_doesnt: All scale domains are hardcoded magic numbers ([3.8, 9.5], [0, 720]) rather than derived from d3.extent/d3.max, so Scaling and Shift metamorphic relations would break with different data; the zone color legend uses .slice(0, 4) leaving Cascadia/Alaska and Himalayan Front unlabeled in the ridgeline panel.
